headline: Body Battery 26 off 5.3h sleep — today's 6km long run stays, but run it dead easy or bank it for tomorrow.
body_state: Recovery failed overnight and the numbers agree: **Body Battery 26** (anything under 30 means the charge never happened), **5.3h sleep** at score 52 — only 12 min REM, 67 min deep — on top of **23h of 14-day sleep debt**. **RHR 51 vs 46 baseline** (+5, an early warning), HRV 41 (balanced), readiness 64, training status Recovery. The deterministic verdict is **red**: protect today, easy or off whatever the plan says. Nothing here is alarming alone, but stacked together they say don't add stress today.
session: Planned: **6km long run** — 5.8km easy @ **4:35–5:03/km**, the shortest long run of the plan, deliberately unstructured, run to feel. On a red-battery morning that shape is right, so keep it — but run the **slow edge (~5:00/km)** and hold HR **under ~146 (75% max)**, truly conversational. The watch stays quiet. If it still feels like RPE 5–6 in the first 2km, cut it short or move it to tomorrow — don't chase pace to prove the block landed.
recent: The pattern is consistent and it's costing you: easy runs keep landing too fast. Tuesday's treadmill matched the 5km easy (green volume, 5.5km) but ran **4:28/km — 9–12s under the window**, closing at 77% max in the grey zone. Wednesday was an unlabelled indoor cardio block that vanishes from load entirely. **Grey-zone middle-intensity is the #1 limiter** (18% easy vs the 80% polarised target). Today is the easiest chance to fix it: slow is the workout.
focus: Run today at the SLOW edge (~5:00/km), HR under 146 — no grey zone on a red-battery cutback morning
Sleep 60 min earlier tonight; chip at the 23h debt before next week's build
Log any indoor cardio with an RPE so it counts toward load instead of disappearing
